mechanism: Zenagamtide/NNC0487-0111 is an investigational unimolecular, long-acting GLP-1 and amylin receptor agonist under development for oral and subcutaneous administration.
phase: Assigned study is Phase 1; diabetes program has completed Phase 2 dose-finding with Phase 3 T2D development planned/initiating in 2026
development_status: NCT07535307 is a recruiting, non-FDA-regulated Phase 1 mechanistic study in adults with type 2 diabetes evaluating once-weekly subcutaneous NNC0487-0111 versus placebo for insulin sensitivity and pancreatic endocrine function through Week 40. The broader NNC0487-0111/amycretin/zenagamtide diabetes program includes completed FDA-regulated Phase 2 dose-finding study NCT06542874 in 448 adults with type 2 diabetes, where Novo Nordisk reported positive headline HbA1c and weight results in November 2025 and stated it planned to initiate a Phase 3 T2D program in 2026. As of this packet, a standalone Phase 3 T2D glycemic-control CT.gov record was not identified, though Phase 3 AMAZE 8 includes participants with overweight/obesity and type 2 diabetes and compares NNC0487-0111 with semaglutide on body-weight endpoints.
expected_launch_window: U.S./EU 2030-2032 if Phase 3 T2D program starts in 2026 and succeeds
clinical_summary: Novo Nordisk reported that in the completed Phase 2 T2D dose-finding trial, once-weekly subcutaneous amycretin achieved dose-dependent HbA1c reductions up to -1.8 percentage points at Week 36 from mean baseline 7.8%, with up to 89.1% reaching HbA1c <7% and up to 76.2% reaching HbA1c <=6.5%. Once-daily oral amycretin achieved HbA1c reductions up to -1.5 percentage points from mean baseline 8.0%, with 77.6% and 62.6% reaching HbA1c <7% and <=6.5%, respectively. Placebo HbA1c changes were -0.2% and -0.4% in the subcutaneous and oral arms. Weight loss was also statistically significant, up to -14.5% with subcutaneous amycretin versus -2.6% with placebo and up to -10.1% with oral amycretin versus -2.5% with placebo, with no weight-loss plateau at Week 36 for higher doses. Differentiation is meaningful because the asset combines GLP-1 and amylin biology in one molecule and has both injectable and oral formulations, but Phase 3 T2D outcomes, cardiovascular/kidney outcomes, and head-to-head data versus semaglutide or tirzepatide are not yet available.
safety_summary: Novo Nordisk reported that subcutaneous and oral amycretin appeared safe and well tolerated in Phase 2 T2D testing, with a profile consistent with incretin and amylin-based therapies; the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal and the vast majority were mild to moderate. No full Phase 2 T2D safety table or Phase 3 T2D safety results were found. GLP-1/T2D analog labels support expected monitoring for thyroid C-cell tumor risk/contraindications, pancreatitis, hypoglycemia when used with insulin or insulin secretagogues, acute kidney injury from volume depletion, severe gastrointestinal events, hypersensitivity, diabetic retinopathy complications, gallbladder disease, aspiration risk during anesthesia/deep sedation, pregnancy considerations, and oral-medication absorption effects.
management_tools: Pharmacy-benefit prior authorization for final labeled type 2 diabetes criteria
Diagnosis confirmation for type 2 diabetes and exclusion of type 1 diabetes, prediabetes-only, metabolic syndrome without T2D, and weight-loss-only use unless separately labeled
Baseline HbA1c and current antidiabetic regimen documentation, including metformin and/or SGLT2 inhibitor use where clinically appropriate and plan design permits
Step or preferred-product positioning against established GLP-1/GIP/GLP-1 options such as semaglutide and tirzepatide when clinically and contractually feasible
Quantity limits aligned to final oral or once-weekly subcutaneous labeled dosing and titration
No concurrent use with other GLP-1, GLP-1/GIP, or incretin-amylin agents unless supported by final labeling
Continuation criteria requiring HbA1c improvement, avoidance of rescue therapy, weight or cardiometabolic benefit where relevant, and tolerability

Safety screening and counseling for pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, severe GI disease, renal risk from dehydration, retinopathy history, pregnancy, thyroid C-cell tumor contraindications, and hypoglycemia risk with insulin/sulfonylureas
evidence_gaps: No Phase 3 T2D efficacy or safety results are available.
A standalone Phase 3 T2D glycemic-control ClinicalTrials.gov record was not identified; Novo Nordisk has stated that Phase 3 T2D development is planned for 2026.
NCT07535307 itself is a Phase 1 mechanistic, non-FDA-regulated study in Germany and should not be interpreted as the pivotal T2D program.
ClinicalTrials.gov does not yet post results for NCT06542874; Phase 2 T2D findings are from Novo Nordisk headline results and upcoming ADA 2026 abstract references.
No direct zenagamtide/NNC0487-0111 U.S. price exists; annual cost uses current Ozempic and Mounjaro analog WAC/list-price sources.
No final selected Phase 3 T2D dose, titration schedule, oral-versus-subcutaneous launch sequencing, cardiovascular outcomes plan, or label positioning is confirmed.

sources.title: Investigating How NNC0487-0111 Regulates Insulin of Adults With Type 2 Diabetes
supports: Assigned asset record NCT07535307; sponsor Novo Nordisk A/S; organization study ID NN9490-8153
Official title evaluates the effect of NNC0487-0111 on insulin sensitivity and pancreatic endocrine function in adults with type 2 diabetes
Recruiting Phase 1 randomized quadruple-masked parallel study with estimated enrollment of 80 adults
Actual start April 10, 2026; estimated primary completion November 11, 2027; estimated completion December 6, 2027
Intervention is NNC0487-0111 administered subcutaneously once weekly via PDS290 pre-filled pen-injectors versus matched placebo
Primary endpoint is change in M-value in hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic clamp from baseline to Week 40
Secondary endpoints include insulin secretion rate, clamp disposition index, beta-cell glucose sensitivity, and HbA1c changes
Eligibility includes adults 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes on stable metformin with permitted SGLT2 inhibitor use and HbA1c thresholds by background therapy
ClinicalTrials.gov oversight lists isFdaRegulatedDrug=false and one recruiting German site

sources.title: Novo Nordisk phase 2 trial with amycretin reports significant weight loss and HbA1c reduction in type 2 diabetes
supports: Amycretin is described as a unimolecular agonist of GLP-1 and amylin receptors intended for once-weekly subcutaneous and once-daily oral administration
Phase 2 T2D trial investigated safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics in 448 people with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor
Dose-finding design included six once-weekly subcutaneous doses from 0.4 mg to 40 mg and three oral daily doses of 6 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg for up to 36 weeks
Subcutaneous amycretin achieved HbA1c reductions up to -1.8% at Week 36 and up to 89.1% of participants achieved HbA1c <7%
Oral amycretin achieved HbA1c reductions up to -1.5% at Week 36 and 77.6% achieved HbA1c <7%
Placebo HbA1c improvements were -0.2% and -0.4% with subcutaneous and oral placebo comparisons
Subcutaneous amycretin achieved body-weight loss up to -14.5% versus -2.6% with placebo; oral amycretin achieved up to -10.1% versus -2.5% with placebo
Safety appeared consistent with incretin and amylin-based therapies; most common adverse events were gastrointestinal and mostly mild to moderate
Novo Nordisk stated it planned to initiate a Phase 3 amycretin program for adults with type 2 diabetes in 2026

Zenagamtide is described as formerly known as amycretin
Zenagamtide is under development by Novo Nordisk for adults with overweight/obesity and adults with type 2 diabetes
Zenagamtide is under investigation for oral and subcutaneous administration
Novo Nordisk states zenagamtide is not approved in the United States, safety and efficacy are not established, and commercial availability is not guaranteed

expected_launch_window.value: U.S./EU 2030-2032 if Phase 3 T2D program starts in 2026 and succeeds
expected_launch_window.method: Used completed Phase 2 T2D study timing, Novo Nordisk's statement that Phase 3 T2D development is planned for 2026, and active Phase 3 obesity/T2D timelines reaching 2028-2029 as contextual comparators.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A T2D launch is unlikely before Phase 3 glycemic-control trials complete, filing occurs, and regulatory review is finished. With Phase 3 planned in 2026 but no standalone T2D Phase 3 CT.gov record identified, 2030-2032 is a planning range rather than a direct company-guided launch date.

annual_cost_range.method: Used current U.S. T2D incretin analog list/WAC prices because zenagamtide is unapproved and unpriced. Low equals Ozempic $1,027.51 x 12 monthly fills. High equals Mounjaro WAC $1,079.77 x 12 monthly fills.
annual_cost_range.explanation: The estimate is a gross analog range before rebates, discounts, patient assistance, adherence, titration wastage, medical visits, labs, or downstream cardiometabolic savings. Final pricing could differ because zenagamtide may have both oral and injectable forms and may launch into a more competitive GLP-1/amylin market.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted the Phase 2 T2D HbA1c and weight headline results, one-molecule GLP-1/amylin mechanism, oral and subcutaneous formulation potential, and future Phase 3 status against lack of pivotal, outcomes, and head-to-head data.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: The Phase 2 signal suggests potential differentiation beyond GLP-1-only therapy, especially if glycemic and weight effects are confirmed in Phase 3. The rating is not High because available T2D evidence is still headline-only, established semaglutide/tirzepatide standards exist, and final dosing/safety positioning is unknown.

budget_impact.method: Combined large U.S. T2D prevalence, chronic incretin-class treatment duration, analog annual gross cost above $12k, expected pharmacy-benefit utilization, and potential use across diabetes plus obesity-adjacent populations.
budget_impact.explanation: If approved with strong HbA1c and weight data, zenagamtide could enter a broad and already high-spend GLP-1 market. Payer controls can limit inappropriate use, but eligible population size and analog pricing support a High budget-impact flag.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed clinical promise and broad-market potential against long launch horizon, no Phase 3 T2D results, no direct price, and existing GLP-1/GIP management infrastructure.
disruption_risk.explanation: The asset could reshape preferred GLP sequencing if Phase 3 confirms a best-in-class profile, but near-term disruption is moderated by current evidence maturity and the fact that payers already manage semaglutide/tirzepatide with PA, step, and quantity-limit tools.

recommended_action.method: Mapped action to positive Phase 2 T2D data, planned 2026 Phase 3 development, high future budget exposure, and unresolved pivotal/label/price details.
recommended_action.explanation: Prepare a GLP-1/amylin policy path now, including T2D diagnosis controls, preferred-product sequencing, and safety monitoring. Defer active formulary contracting or launch controls until Phase 3 T2D trials, dose selection, route strategy, filing timing, and price are clearer.

quality_flags: Asset naming is evolving: ClinicalTrials.gov uses NNC0487-0111, Novo's 2025 Phase 2 announcement uses amycretin, and Novo's May 2026 ADA release describes zenagamtide as formerly known as amycretin.
The assigned NCT07535307 record is Phase 1, non-FDA-regulated, and located in Germany; it is mechanistic support rather than a pivotal T2D study.
Novo Nordisk has stated Phase 3 T2D development is planned for 2026, but a standalone Phase 3 T2D glycemic-control ClinicalTrials.gov record was not identified as of 2026-05-28.
NCT06542874 has no posted ClinicalTrials.gov results; Phase 2 T2D efficacy and safety details are based on Novo Nordisk headline results and ADA 2026 presentation listings.
No direct zenagamtide/NNC0487-0111 price was found; annual cost uses Ozempic and Mounjaro analog list/WAC prices.
Annual cost estimates are gross analog amounts and do not reflect rebates, net prices, patient assistance, differential oral/injectable pricing, or future GLP-1 price changes.
No FDA label, direct payer policy, cardiovascular outcomes evidence, kidney outcomes evidence, or final Phase 3 dose/route strategy is available for zenagamtide.
